confirmed.title: Flag-day receipt_root/logs_root fork under mixed validator versions
confirmed.trigger: Mixed validator set (some pre-#936, some post-#936) processing a block with any event-bearing tx, e.g. Actor(ExecuteActor{actor:A, handler:"handle"}) whose handler calls emit_event("t", b"d"). Post-#936 <Write for TransactionReceipt>::write prepends 20-byte emitter A in the events loop and compute_logs_root prepends A before topic/data; pre-#936 omits both. r.encode() bytes differ → compute_receipt_root (merkle_utils.rs:33, keccak over r.encode()) yields different receipt_root per version. block.receipt_root committed by the proposer mismatches the recompute on the other-version validators → application.rs verify() rejects (lines 2058-2062/2206-2213) → block cannot finalize across the mixed set = consensus fork/stall.
confirmed.reason: The emitter is added unconditionally to both the receipt events codec and compute_logs_root with no version/activation-height gate (unlike #848's u64::MAX gate or #934's omit-at-default), so receipt_root and logs_root are not byte-identical across pre/post-#936 binaries for any event-bearing tx. receipt_root is consensus state (block digest + verify() equality check), so mixed-version rollout diverges. This is an intended flag-day change: the divergence is real and only mitigable operationally via coordinated simultaneous activation — needs_human, not fixable by any guard present in this diff.

confirmed.title: Unconditional emitter in logs_root/receipt_root/state_root with no activation-height gate → partial-rollout fork
confirmed.trigger: Mixed-version validator set at the same height: validator A on pre-#936 binary, B on post-#936. Any block with one event-emitting tx (e.g. actor calls emit_event("x", b"y")). A encodes the receipt's event as (topic,data); B prepends the 20-byte emitter. compute_receipt_root hashes keccak256(receipt.encode()) (merkle_utils.rs:33), so receipt.encode() differs -> receipt_root differs -> block digest differs -> verify() rejects the peer's proposal -> consensus halt/fork. Parallel divergence via logs_root (receipt field) and via ActorEvent codec into actor_events state_root.
confirmed.reason: The emitter is added unconditionally to compute_logs_root, compute_bloom, TransactionReceipt Write/Read/EncodeSize, rlp_encode, and ActorEvent Write/Read — with NO version byte, NO has_remaining() optional-suffix, and NO activation-height gate. Verified receipt_root is consensus-bound (compute_receipt_root over full receipt.encode(); state_invariants.rs:715 asserts propose==verify) and that emitter enters that encoding on every event. Golden KATs were deliberately recomputed, so this is an intentional flag-day, not an oversight. Unlike the opt-in field additions in #848/#934 that stayed byte-identical to legacy (u64::MAX height gate / omit-at-default), the emitter is present on every event so no configuration reproduces legacy bytes — a height gate is the only fork-safe rollout mechanism and it is absent. The hypothesis is therefore unrefutable: a partial rollout WILL fork. Disposition is needs_human / coordinated simultaneous rollout (or add an activation-height gate) rather than a logic-correctness fix.

confirmed.title: Old persisted receipts/ActorEventList mis-decode after upgrade (no version gate on emitter)
confirmed.dimension: determinism / persisted-state backward-compat (readback across in-place upgrade)
confirmed.trigger: Pre-#936 node persisted an ActorEventList (e.g. TOKEN_REGISTRY_SYSTEM_ACTOR, one event topic="Transfer" 8B + 32B data) into state_db; operator swaps binary to #936 without wiping QMDB. Post-upgrade ActorEvent::read_cfg reads block_height(8)+tx_hash(32) OK, then Address::read consumes 20 bytes = topic varint-len(1) + "Transfer"(8) + first 11B of data as a bogus emitter; the following Vec::<u8>::read_cfg(topic, RangeCfg 0..=256) reads a length from mid-payload -> exceeds range or from_utf8 fails -> StateValue::read returns Err. Result: (a) RPC get_actor_events(TOKEN_REGISTRY) (rpc/handlers/chain.rs:1691) errors instead of returning history; (b) next block's append_actor_events (accounts.rs:1022 read-modify-write) hits the same Err, caught by warn! in speculative.rs, so that actor's new events are dropped -- permanently, since every future append re-reads the same undecodable value. Same misframe hits get_transaction_receipt for pre-#936 receipts (events loop reads emitter unconditionally, no has_remaining gate).
confirmed.reason: The unconditional emitter read before topic (no version/discriminant gate) genuinely misframes any pre-#936 ActorEvent/TransactionReceipt on readback -- a real backward-compat break confirmed by exact byte trace, and inconsistent with the codebase's own MAILBOX_MESSAGE V1/V2 discriminant-first backward-compat pattern. BUT the fork/halt part of the hypothesis is refuted: (1) the effect is deterministic across a uniformly-upgraded validator set (identical old bytes + identical decoder -> identical Err/warn on every node) so no divergence; (2) receipts are stored in a non-merkleized side DB (state_key.rs:48; blockchain_storage.rs:773 explicitly "state root / consensus not affected"), and logs_root/receipt_root/state_root are computed from in-memory events, never by re-decoding stored receipts -- so the claimed "receipt-root recompute over historical receipts" path does not exist; (3) no halt: the decode Err is ?-propagated and swallowed by warn! at the append site, and receipts are regenerated on block replay. Residual impact is node-local: pre-#936 event-log/receipt RPC returns errors/garbage and pre-existing actor event logs silently stop accepting new events. Real but low severity, non-consensus, and moot if flag-day means a fresh-genesis relaunch.

confirmed.title: Unlisted System-instruction events are now persisted under placeholder tx.from (previously dropped) — silent state_root semantics change
confirmed.trigger: Block with a SubmitProposal tx (or any governance/CIP-34/CIP-7/RAS/runner-delegation System instruction that pushes to self.system_events, e.g. topics governance.proposal.submitted, cip34.IntentSettled, cip7.stream.seal_partial_accepted). execute_transaction drains system_events as placeholder (tx.from, topic, data); in speculative.rs system_event_emitter(&instruction, tx.from) hits `_ => None` for these non-enumerated variants, so `events` retain emitter=tx.from, `if !events.is_empty()` runs, BTreeMap groups under tx.from, and append_actor_events(tx.from, …) pushes an ActorEvent into state_pending → state_root (confirmed: state_root = speculative_state_root_for_pending(&state_pending), speculative.rs:2405-2414; append_actor_events writes state_pending, accounts.rs:392-393). OLD inline match returned actor_addr=None for these (`_ => None`) and the `if let Some(actor_addr)` guard skipped append entirely, so these events were only in receipt_root/logs_root, never in actor_events/state_root. Net: NEW state_root gains actor_events entries under the EOA submitter that OLD semantics excluded, and the event is mis-attributed to tx.from rather than its true owner (e.g. GOVERNANCE_SYSTEM_ACTOR 0x09), polluting the submitter's /actor events log and binding emitter=tx.from in logs_root.
confirmed.reason: The hypothesis holds as a real behavioral change. actor_events is merkleized into state_root (speculative.rs:2410 via state_pending; append_actor_events pushes state_pending). For System instructions outside the enumerated match (governance, CIP-34, CIP-7, RAS, delegation — all confirmed to push to self.system_events), OLD code's inline actor_addr match returned None and the `if let Some(actor_addr)` guard skipped the append, so those events never entered state_root; NEW code's system_event_emitter also returns None but the placeholder (tx.from,…) emitter set in transaction.rs survives, so the unconditional `if !events.is_empty()` BTreeMap-persist now appends them under tx.from, growing state_root with entries OLD semantics excluded and mis-attributing system events to the EOA submitter (contradicting the PR's own true-emitter thesis). Severity is mid, not high: the whole PR is flag-day (unconditional receipt-codec change + recomputed goldens), and the new path is deterministic (BTreeMap order, tx.from), so all upgraded honest nodes compute identical state_root — no honest-node fork beyond the coordinated activation the PR already requires. It is a genuine, unstated expansion of consensus-state content plus a mis-attribution, but not an independent fork/split. logs_root/persist stay mutually consistent (both use the same post-normalization events binding), so no internal inconsistency fork either.
